seal.hash_rule: sha256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of the predictions array
seal.note: Pre-registered 2026-11-14 00:58 UTC for 27 games (2026-11-14..2026-11-17) from the 2026-11-14 snapshot. Spread/total are model projections in half-point increments; no market price was available to this build, so no bet is asserted — only our number and the trigger level. These predictions must not be edited after tip-off: settle them with nba2.pipeline.settle. Verify the digest with `python -c "from nba2.models import ledger; print(ledger.verify(r'...'))"`.

ratings.title: Team ratings table (the model's only inputs)
ratings.blurb: The two win-loss columns are INDEPENDENT measurements and they are printed side by side for exactly that reason: the model runs on the 2026-11-13 third-party snapshot (the left-hand pair), while the right-hand pair is the league's own table read on 2026-11-14 — NBA.com/standings. They differ for 18 clubs because the nine 2026-11-13 games were played in between — an aged snapshot, not a transcription error. PS/G, PA/G and SRS could still not be pulled from an official endpoint (FLAG-RAT-01); the 'Margins & Stats' section of nba.com/standings does not render them for a non-browser client.
ratings.source_note: Left column: data/raw/team_ratings_2026-11-13.json (third-party Basketball-Reference snapshot). Right column: data/raw/official_standings_2026-11-14.json (official NBA.com).

injury_delta_release.title: Injury release delta — 19:30 ET (published before) vs 05:00 a.m ET (published now)
injury_delta_release.blurb: An injury report is re-issued several times a day and a player who was Questionable at 19:30 can be Out at 05:00. The diff is published so the churn is visible instead of hidden behind whichever release happened to be latest.
injury_delta_release.source_note: Both documents are official; the diff is computed in-repo.

calibration.title: Model parameters — derived, not assumed
calibration.blurb: These are the only two structural numbers the whole site depends on. Both are fitted against the verified standings snapshot; where the fit is weak we say so instead of quietly picking a convention.
calibration.source_note: Inputs: data/raw/team_ratings_2026-11-13.json (third-party). Win-loss verified three ways: NBA.com game cards (28/30 visible in that capture; TOR/WAS = FLAG-SLATE-02), the prior session's independent read (30/30), and a fresh upstream re-read on 2026-11-14 (30/30 identical — data/raw/ratings_recheck_2026-11-14.json).

values.method: least-squares fit of (sigma, hca) to the 30 verified win totals, grid 6.00-25.00 step 0.25 then refine step 0.01
values.sanity: NBA game margins are widely reported near 13-14 pts; our fit is independent of that

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: same joint fit
values.sanity: league home win rate implied by verified home/road splits = 51.1%; that rate alone implies a smaller h than the joint fit

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: unweighted mean of the 30 teams' PS/G

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: tau^2 = max(0, Var(SRS) - mean(se^2)), se = sigma/sqrt(games)
values.sanity: mean se = 3.99; shrinkage lambda therefore ~0.74-0.78 per team

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: model win total error at the optimum

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.ratings
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Calibration + shrinkage computed from the verified snapshot at build time.

values.method: NOT fitted: set before any game-level totals existed (official finals history now sits in the backtest tree; re-fitting is an owner decision, S-04); used only inside the parlay sensitivity band
values.sanity: level-sensitive, so parlay output is reported as a ratio, not a price

luck.title: Skill / luck decomposition
luck.blurb: Luck here means: wins beyond what a normal-margin model fitted to this same table implies, scaled by the binomial noise of that team's schedule size. The two right-hand columns are deliberately blank — the close/blowout split we fetched does not balance league-wide, so we refuse to use it for a luck claim.
luck.source_note: Derived from the same verified table; no external source for the decomposition.

lines.title: Originated lines for every game in the window
lines.blurb: Spread/total are our numbers, quoted in half-point increments so nothing pushes. Positive consensus margin = home team favoured. No column here is a market price: with no odds feed these lines cannot be compared to a book, and we do not pretend otherwise.

picks.title: Picks — expressed as triggers, not as 'bets'
picks.blurb: A pick with no price is a guess. So each row states the number the market would have to show before our line justifies action, and the stake stays 0% until an odds feed exists. This is the honest shape of a line-origination desk before it has execution. The table covers the pick window from the snapshot's as-of date forward (today + 3 days max); the day-before context games are priced on the Lines page for calibration only.
picks.source_note: Triggers = our line ± 1.5 pts (unratified hurdle, see FLAG-LINE-03).

values.trigger: home spread ≥ +7.5 → take home; home spread ≤ +4.5 → take away
values.total_trigger: market total ≤ 233.0 → OVER; market total ≥ 236.0 → UNDER

Covers 11/13 games plus the first official statuses for the 11/14 slate (five teams had still not submitted at this release).

injuries_window.title: Official NBA injury report — 2026-11-14 day-before designations (11/13/26 19:30 ET release)
injuries_window.blurb: First official designations for the 2026-11-14 slate: five teams had filed by the 5 p.m. ET day-before deadline, five had not (NOT YET SUBMITTED). Game-day reports on 11/14 (11 a.m.-1 p.m. local) can still change these statuses. The three impact columns are blank by policy — the report contains no minutes or production data, so any number there would be invented. P(plays) is our modelling convention for counting bodies, not a league probability.

availability_window.title: Availability coverage of the sealed pick window (2026-11-14 → 11-17)
availability_window.blurb: Computed from every official injury release this repository holds (11/13 16:15 ET, 11/13 19:30 ET and 11/14 05:00 a.m ET), never inferred. 'Coverage' is the share of team-slots carrying any official participation designation at capture time; it rises as later releases are ingested. The lines for this window were originated from the 2026-11-13 snapshot and sealed; availability data refreshes around them. A team that appears as NOT YET SUBMITTED in one release and files designations in a later one is counted once, as filed.

gameflow.title: Game flow — what the slate tells us, and everything it does not

Right of the divider: blank, because in-game flow needs play-by-play, lineups and foul data that this repository does not have. A 'game flow analysis' that narrates those four columns without the data is storytelling, and it is how books get paid.

anomalies.title: Slate irregularities found while transcribing
anomalies.blurb: Recorded, not fixed. Each of these would corrupt an automated pipeline that trusted the pattern instead of the value.
anomalies.source_note: First recorded from https://www.nba.com/schedule retrieved 2026-11-13 22:39 UTC; dispositions updated where the 2026-11-14 capture resolves the question.

values.observation: Identical matchup and arena (Scotiabank Arena) as 0022600241 on 2026-11-15, two days apart. Both were read from the same official schedule page.
values.disposition: RESOLVED BY THE 2026-11-14 CAPTURE — the official page renders both games as distinct entries with distinct official game IDs, so this is a genuine schedule entry, not a duplicate card. Now inside the pick window; the rest/B2B consequences are priced by game flow and flagged.

parlays_xg.title: Cross-game parlays, and what stacking costs
parlays_xg.blurb: Two different games: the product rule is nearly right, so cross-game parlays are the safe place to express multiple views. Same game: the product rule is off by 13–26% on the ten quoted games above, which is larger than the entire edge a good model earns. And every leg you add multiplies the book's hold — arithmetic that needs no data to check.
parlays_xg.source_note: ρ = 0 assumed for cross-game (FLAG-CORR-05); -110 is a labelled placeholder price, not a quote.

gates.title: Validation gates — specification
gates.blurb: A strategy must clear all ten to be promoted and to receive rewards. Most are still blocked by missing data; G-04 now has measured evidence and FAILS it, G-07 is measured PASS in the backtest tree — which is the real status of this project and the reason the leaderboard pays nothing.

values.name: Sample size
values.rule: >= 300 settled bets for team markets; >= 500 for player props.
values.why: At -110 a 55% bettor needs roughly 300 bets before the standard error (sqrt(p(1-p)/n) ~ 2.9%) stops swamping a 5-point edge. Below this the leaderboard is ranking noise.
values.source: derived from the binomial standard error at p=0.55 — see research/05-skill-vs-luck.md
values.blocked: No settled bets yet. The ledger opened with the 2026-11-13 slate and was re-sealed for 2026-11-14..17.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Closing line value (CLV)
values.rule: Mean CLV vs. closing number > 0 with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0.
values.why: CLV is the single least-luck-dependent measure of whether a line beats the market.
values.source: BLOCKED: requires a licensed odds feed (requirements R-101)
values.blocked: No market prices captured. Our lines are published, but nothing to beat them yet.

source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Probability calibration
values.rule: Brier score <= 0.245 on settled games AND calibration slope in [0.85, 1.15] AND intercept in [-0.10, 0.10].
values.why: 0.25 is the Brier score of always forecasting 50%; a line-originator must beat that and be calibrated, otherwise the stake sizing is fiction.
values.source: derived: Brier (1950) definition; threshold is our own proposal (unratified)

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Line accuracy vs. naive baselines
values.rule: Mean absolute error of our spread must beat BOTH baselines: (a) 0.0 spread, (b) raw point-differential-per-game, by >= 0.30 points.
values.why: A line that only reproduces the standings' scoring margin adds no work; if shrinkage and schedule adjustment do not reduce error, delete the model.
values.source: derived from the snapshot baselines in nba2.models.gates
values.blocked: Measured evidence now exists (backtest tree, 139 official finals 2026-10-20 to 11-12, leakage-asserted walk-forward): margin MAE 12.17 vs the 0.0-spread baseline 13.27 — better, p=0.35; straight-up 62.6% vs point-differential baseline 64.0% — NOT better. The 0.30-pt bar is not cleared: G-04 FAILS on measured data. See backtest/pages/validation-gates.html.

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Luck removal
values.rule: Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, fixed seed) 95% CI of ROI excludes 0; t-stat >= 2.0; and the luck-adjusted PnL (each bet replaced by its model-expected PnL, variance kept) must not reverse the sign.
values.why: Separates 'won' from 'right'. A strategy whose PnL is explained by a few lucky bad beats fails here even if the record is positive.
values.source: derived: standard bootstrap / t-test; see research/05-skill-vs-luck.md

source.name: Derived: nba2.models.lines
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Lines are arithmetic on the calibrated ratings; reproduce with `python -m nba2.pipeline.build_site_data`.

values.name: Multiple-testing control
values.rule: Across every strategy ever evaluated in the same window, apply Holm-Bonferroni to the CLV t-tests and require the Deflated Sharpe Ratio > 0.
values.why: A leaderboard with N trials will produce a 'best' strategy by pure search. Punishing the number of tries is the only defence.
values.source: derived: Holm (1979); Deflated Sharpe = Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014) formulation
values.blocked: Requires G-02 inputs and a complete trial ledger (see S-11).

values.name: Walk-forward, no lookahead
values.rule: Every feature timestamped at or before tip-off; train on the first 70% of the window, test on the final 30%; test MAE must not exceed full-window MAE by more than 25%.
values.why: Ratings built from a standings snapshot include future games for the teams that played earlier; that leak is silent and fatal.
values.source: derived from our own ingest design (see research/01-line-origination.md 'point-in-time')
values.status: evaluable — measured PASS (backtest tree); root fit still snapshot-based
values.blocked: The current snapshot is a single as-of standings table, which is NOT point-in-time for games inside the week it covers — that caveat still applies to the root ratings fit. The dedicated walk-forward re-implementation (backtest/engine/walkforward.py, leakage asserted by test) MEASURED PASS on 139 official finals: test MAE does not exceed full-window MAE by more than the 25% threshold. See backtest/pages/walk-forward.html.

values.name: Parameter robustness
values.rule: Re-price the slate over the full sensitivity box of every unratified parameter; a pick is only published if its side is unchanged in >= 90% of the grid.
values.why: If a 10% change in sigma flips the pick, the pick is a parameter, not a signal.

values.name: Cost and capacity
values.rule: Survive -110 vig, 1% hard-cap stake, 25% Kelly, and a re-quote of the model at the reference price minus 0.25 points of expected slippage.
values.why: Lines that only win before the vig, or before you move size, are not tradeable.

values.name: Availability-adjustment guardrail
values.rule: If a player on the official report with an Out/Doubtful status cannot be mapped to a quantified minutes delta, the line is published availability-blind and the game is marked INJURY-BLIND. No bet may be Tier A on an injury-blind game after the 13:00 ET report on game day.

params.title: Every tunable number in the system, and whether anyone has justified it
params.blurb: This is the anti-overfitting page: any value whose status is not 'derived' or 'verified' is a place where a human could have cheated, so they are listed with their bands.

values.rationale: SD of a team's per-game margin. Searched over [6, 25]; the value used is the least-squares optimum against observed wins, so it is a fitted quantity, not an assumption.

repo_review.title: Repository review
repo_review.blurb: Reviewed from the git history and the working tree, not from a summary of it.
repo_review.source_note: All findings also recorded in COORDINATION.md

values.finding: The repo began as a single 6-byte README.md containing '# NBA2'. There was no code, data, CI, licence or Pages configuration.
values.evidence: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 623b4c2` → README.md only; `git show 623b4c2:README.md` → '# NBA2'
values.action: Nothing to inherit; everything below is net-new. Documented so no later session claims prior work existed.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: No LICENSE file at any commit.
values.evidence: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 7fa2a24` contains no LICENSE
values.action: FLAGGED, not fixed: adding a licence is an owner decision, especially while third-party data is embedded (see Q-18).

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Prior `data/injuries.json` published numeric impacts ('Starter out — ~0 min (vs. ~34 MPG season avg)', '-100% scoring/rebounding/playmaking output') that appear in no source. The official report has no minutes or MPG column.
values.evidence: `git show 821c175:data/injuries.json` keys: player, team, status, injury, game, minutesImpact, productionImpact, verified — no source field; report columns are Game Date, Game Time, Matchup, Team, Player, Status, Reason
values.action: Impact columns replaced with explicit blanks + FLAG-INJ-02. Rows kept and re-sourced to the official PDF.

source.name: This repository (git history)
source.class_label: Official NBA.com / NBA CDN
source.note: Repo review facts: commit list, file tree.

values.finding: Prior `data/strategies.json` attributed correlation coefficients (r ≈ 0.82, r ≈ 0.65) to https://www.nba.com/stats/help/faq, a help/FAQ page that contains no such values. The rows were labelled 'unverified' but still carried a source link that implies verification.
values.evidence: field `source` on those rows vs. the page's actual content
values.action: Removed. Correlations are now computed where possible (r(SRS, margin/G)) and blank elsewhere; a misattributed source is worse than no source.

values.finding: Prior `data/picks.json` invented synthetic game IDs (GAME-20261113-001) for fixtures that have official IDs, and covered only 3 of the 9 games on 11/13.
values.evidence: `git show 821c175:data/picks.json` vs `https://www.nba.com/schedule`
values.action: Replaced with official IDs; slate now 31/31 games for the window.

values.action: Consolidated to one workflow so a run cannot be cancelled mid-deploy by its twin (T-14).

values.finding: I-07: home/away back-to-back and 3-in-4 flags substring-matched the game date against the whole pair/sequence string ('d1+d2', 'd1->d2->d3'), so the FIRST night of a consecutive pair was also flagged as a B2B (e.g. DAL on 11/14 ahead of its 11/15 game; POR on 11/16 ahead of 11/17). Published values were over-counted, not fabricated.
values.evidence: nba2/models/gameflow.py::game_flow_inputs before the 2026-11-14 fix; reproduced in the refreshed build's 11/14 rows (DAL away_b2b=YES with no 11/13 game).
values.action: Detection anchored on the second night of a pair and the third game of a 3-in-4 sequence; regression tests added (TestGameFlowB2B); FLAG-FLOW-03 discloses that pre-refresh rows carried inflated values.

values.action: Refreshed in this session: new official slate capture (36 games, 11/13 context + 11/14-17), freshest injury release (11/13 19:30 ET, 122 rows incl. first 11/14 statuses), ratings re-check (30/30 identical), new sealed ledger of 27 picks for 11/14-17 with a refuse-to-seal guard under 6h to tip. values.finding: crosscheck CC-SEAL-04 reports five sealed predictions as 'not tipped after the snapshot'. It compares calendar dates, not timestamps, and it is wrong: the 2026-11-14 ledger was sealed 2026-11-14T00:58:54Z and the earliest game in it tips 2026-11-14 19:00 ET = 2026-11-15T00:00Z. The true minimum lead time across all 27 predictions is 23.02 hours.
values.evidence: `python3` over data/raw/ledger/sealed-2026-11-14.json: header.sealed_at_utc = 2026-11-14T00:58:54Z; min over predictions of (date+time_et at UTC-5) - seal = 23.02 h (0022600231), 23.52 h (0022600232), 24.02 h (0022600233/34).
values.action: Logged, not fixed: tools/crosscheck_site.py is owned by session arena/5b80b88a. The check should compare datetimes (tip_utc > seal_utc), not dates. This also answers Q-31's underlying worry in the affirmative for this ledger — it really was sealed before every tip.

requirements.title: Requirements register
requirements.blurb: Every requirement in the brief, decomposed to something a reviewer can say yes/no to. Status is only 'met' when the artefact exists in the repository.
requirements.source_note: Decomposed from the project brief (Arena session request of 2026-11-13) plus the engineering requirements needed to satisfy it. Status is a self-assessment against files in this repository, reviewed by a human owner next.

questions.title: Open questions — the decision list
questions.blurb: Ordered by how much money a wrong answer costs, not by how interesting they are. Each row states what is already known so nobody re-asks it.
questions.source_note: Each row is a decision, not a curiosity: it says what we already have, what is missing, how to close it, and what changes in the model once it is answered. Anything I could resolve from an official source this session was resolved instead of asked.

values.question: Which odds source are we measuring against — and are we allowed to store its closing prices?
values.have: The full slate, our lines, and the knowledge that NBA.com renders odds client-side only and picks.nba.com publishes none.
values.missing: Any licensed book price, opening or closing, for any sport.
values.how: Owner picks a vendor (theScore Sportsdata/Odds API, Sportradar, or a sportsbook affiliate feed) and confirms storage rights; then add an ingest to data/raw.
values.impact: Everything. Without it there is no 'edge', no CLV, no gate G-02, no stake sizing, and no reason to prefer our number over a coin flip.

values.question: Is the product a line-setting desk or a betting-picks desk?
values.have: Both capabilities sketched: pricing engine (works) and bet selection with triggers (needs prices).
values.missing: Owner decision on primary objective.
values.how: Answer in one sentence; it changes which gate blocks promotion.
values.impact: A line-setting desk is graded on MAE/calibration and is buildable today with zero market data. A picks desk is not buildable until Q-01 is resolved.

values.impact: Kelly fraction, promotion criteria (G-09) and the reward pool's meaning.

values.question: Do we accept that game-day injury data arrives too late for a T-3 publication?
values.have: The official report's structure and cadence, plus proof: in the 11/13 16:15 ET release, all ten Nov 14 teams were 'NOT YET SUBMITTED'.
values.missing: Whether you want T-3 lines (injury-blind) only, or a T-0 re-issue after the 13:00 ET report.
values.how: Owner decision; implement as a second daily build at 13:30 ET.
values.impact: Determines whether '3 days in advance' is a feature or a self-inflicted handicap. Our lines currently apply no injury adjustment at all.

values.missing: An accessible official source or a licensed alternative.
values.how: Test from the CI runner (different network than this sandbox); if still blocked, evaluate a commercial feed.
values.impact: Props, prop combos, injury impact, and the margin/total correlation all sit behind this one answer.

values.question: Do Emirates NBA Cup group games belong in the same distribution as ordinary regular-season games?
values.have: The 11/13 slate is entirely Cup group play, and Cup games count for group standing with different incentives (winning by margin matters as a tiebreaker).
values.missing: Historical evidence on whether Cup games differ in pace, rotations or margin distribution.
values.how: Split the results snapshot by game_type once R-103 lands and test pace/margin differences.
values.impact: If Cup games differ, today's entire slate is mis-calibrated and the model needs a game-type effect or an exclusion rule.

values.missing: A decision, because they currently control which games are actionable.
values.how: Owner reviews the Parameters page and either accepts or edits config.py.

values.have: Reliability weights ~0.74-0.78 and a fitted RMSE of 1.31 wins vs 2.78 baseline.
values.missing: Your risk policy for early-season modelling.
values.how: Owner decision; a hard rule could be 'no Tier A before 25 games'.

values.question: What is the definition of 'removing luck' you will accept as a gate?
values.have: Four candidate mechanisms implemented: bootstrap CI on PnL, t-stat ≥ 2, calibration slope, and rewards weighted on CLV/accuracy rather than PnL.
values.missing: Whether you also require a variance-reduction metric (e.g. Sharpe of residualised PnL) or a holdout-only payout.
values.how: Owner picks; add to gates.
values.impact: Changes which strategies can win the leaderboard, and therefore what gets built next.

values.missing: Whether volume should carry weight (e.g. minimum coverage per slate).
values.how: Owner decision.
values.impact: A 'bet three games a season' strategy can look elite without a volume term.

values.question: What is the correct treatment of a two-way/G-League assignment listed on the injury report?

values.missing: Whether those absences should affect a rotation-floor model identically to injury.
values.how: Owner decision; implement as a reason-class weighting in injuries.py.

values.have: It currently reports project state and blockers first, because that is the truth today.
values.missing: Whether you want a picks-first summary as soon as prices exist.
values.how: Owner decision; the summary is generated, so it is a template change.

values.question: Which numbers on this site would change your decision if they moved by 10%?
values.have: A sensitivity band for every structural parameter, and a stability fraction per line.
values.missing: Your decision threshold — currently the model assumes ±10% matters, and suppresses a pick when it does.
values.how: Owner states a threshold; encode in G-08.
values.impact: This is the difference between a research dashboard and a betting system.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: When a published snapshot goes stale, should the site keep showing it (labelled) or withhold the page entirely?
values.have: Proof of the failure mode, measured today: the v2 team table matches the pre-11/13-finals state 30/30 and current official standings only 12/30, while the page still advertises a 30/30 live match. The nine 11/13 finals were played while the table was frozen.
values.missing: A rule. Nothing in the build currently compares a published row against a fresher official capture, so staleness can only be caught by a human reading two pages.
values.how: Set a maximum snapshot age per table (records: 1 day; prices: 15 minutes; injuries: to the next official filing). Add a staleness gate to nba2/v2/check.py that fails when a row is older than its limit, and render stale rows with an explicit 'as of' badge instead of a MATCH badge.
values.impact: Without it the site can show a table it calls verified that is provably wrong the next morning. This is the single highest-cost defect found this session because it is silent.
values.evidence: nba2/v2/live.py::staleness()

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Is a 4-game, 0-loss forecast worth publishing at all, and what is the minimum n before a strategy may be ranked?
values.have: The first real out-of-sample result in the repository: nba2/data/picks.json committed 83 minutes before tip, 4 distinct games bet, all 4 won (S1 moneyline and S2 spread fired on the same games, so 8 recorded wins are 4 games). Model called the winner in 5 of 9 games; always-home would have got 7.
values.missing: The promotion threshold. Existing gates want 30 settled bets, which is the right order of magnitude but has never been ratified as a number the owner will accept waiting for.
values.how: Owner ratifies: minimum n (proposal: 100 settled, to have power to detect a 3-point edge), and whether a 4-0 start is allowed to be displayed at all once n is known to be inadequate.
values.impact: 4-0 is exactly the result that would get a bettor to increase stakes. Publishing it without the n=4 context would make the site a machine for manufacturing false confidence.
values.evidence: nba2/v2/live.py::grade()

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Should a per-strategy win rate be allowed to count the same game twice when two strategies fire on it?
values.have: The measured overlap: of 4 graded games, all 4 were bet by both S1_MarginFavorite and S2_SpreadValue. Per-strategy hit rates stay valid; any portfolio or leaderboard return that sums them double-counts the games.
values.missing: A portfolio accounting rule: whether the leaderboard scores strategies independently (as now) or scores the union of positions actually held.
values.how: Owner decision. Independent scoring is simpler and correct for ranking hypotheses; union scoring is correct for describing what a bankroll would have done. They answer different questions and the site currently only implements one.
values.impact: If rewards are paid on summed per-strategy results, two correlated strategies split one result twice and the reward pool systematically overpays correlation, which is the thing the project exists to price.
values.evidence: nba2/v2/live.py::grade()['duplicate_accounting']

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Does a team rating that is computed from a frozen standings table need to be re-fitted per slate, or is a same-day snapshot accurate enough?
values.have: A measured comparison on 9 graded games: the model's margin MAE was 11.46 against 13.33 for predicting a tie, but its winner accuracy (5/9) was no better than a naive net-rating baseline computed from the same frozen table (5/9).
values.missing: A rebuilt rating on post-11/13 data. That requires re-running the whole pipeline against today's official standings, which is a data refresh, not a code change.
values.how: Refresh data/raw with the 30 current records captured today (already in audit/2026-11-14/official_inputs_2026-11-14.json), rebuild, re-seal a new ledger, and compare. Until then no claim about which estimator is better is supported.
values.impact: Decides whether the daily cadence is a real requirement or a nicety: if a one-day-old table costs accuracy, the nightly job is load-bearing.
values.evidence: nba2/v2/live.py::grade()['side_accuracy']

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Should the unreachable v1 tree be retired, and who signs off on deleting a published surface?
values.have: A direct probe of the live site on 2026-11-14: pages/executive-summary.html and pages/session-audit.html both return HTTP 404, while site/-only data/teams.json returns 200 with v2 content. Exactly one tree is served — site/. The Pages API still reports build_type=legacy, source=main/, which does not describe what is served.
values.missing: Permission to retire the v1 tree. It is regenerated, linted and parity-checked on every push and contains records that were true only before the 11/13 finals, but no reader can reach it.
values.how: Move root index.html, pages/**, flagged.html and data/site.json under archive/ with a dated note, drop them from ci.yml's parity step, and keep the v2 build as the only generator. Deleting nothing is also a valid answer if the archive is clearly labelled.
values.impact: Every minute spent verifying the v1 tree is spent on a surface nobody reads, and its stale numbers keep appearing in repo-wide audits and confusing later sessions.
values.evidence: audit/2026-11-14/deploy_probe.json

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: How is a pick's price recorded if no odds feed will ever be licensed?
values.have: Every graded signal in nba2/data/picks.json lacks a price field entirely, so win/loss is measurable and profit is not. Reported -110 would make every number in this project an assumption about a book.
values.missing: Either a licensed feed, or a decision to accept manual price entry, or a decision that the project only ever publishes winners and never PnL.
values.how: Owner picks one of three. Option three is viable and cheap: publish hit rates and CLV-free triggers, and never claim a return.
values.impact: Decides whether the leaderboard competition can ever have a cash-relevant reward, or is permanently an accuracy contest.
values.evidence: nba2/data/picks.json: no american_odds field on any of 21 signals

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Who is allowed to move the build stamp, and how should a refresh be recorded?
values.have: The stamp is now derived from the newest retrieved_at_utc inside the committed snapshots (2026-11-14 01:05 UTC as of this build), so it cannot drift on a rebuild. An explicit NBA2_BUILD_STAMP override exists but nothing in CI sets it.
values.missing: A refresh procedure. Today a snapshot is refreshed by a human or a workflow writing a new file under data/raw with a new retrieved_at_utc; nothing records who authorised the refresh or which official page it came from at run time.
values.how: Make the nightly refresh the only writer of data/raw, have it write retrieved_at_utc plus the exact source URL per file, and forbid hand edits in CI by checking that every new snapshot carries a retrieval record. The override then never needs to be used.
values.impact: Without it 'as of' is only as trustworthy as the last hand edit, which is the class of problem F-029 came from.
values.evidence: nba2/pipeline/build_site_data.py::_content_stamp

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Is the model any good? We now have nine games graded against official results — is that an answer?
values.have: A graded card for 2026-11-13 (data/graded_2026-11-13.json): margin MAE 12.97 vs 13.33 for a no-information baseline, total MAE 12.90 vs 16.20, winner calls 5/9, AUROC 0.93. The inputs are strictly point-in-time, proven by the identity (committed ratings W-L) + (the nine results) = official NBA.com standings, 30/30.
values.missing: Statistical significance. Permutation p = 0.95 (margin) and p = 0.40 (total); the Wilson 95% CI on the hit rate is 26.7%-81.1%. About 1,565 graded games are needed to detect a 55% hit rate at 5% significance with 80% power.
values.how: Keep grading every completed slate with the same script and re-test when the sample supports it. Do not promote a strategy or pay a reward before then — gate G-01 requires 300 settled bets and nothing changes that.
values.impact: Decides whether the originated lines are worth the effort at all. The honest answer today is: unproven, directionally mildly positive on totals, untested on margins.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Should every slate be sealed before its first tip, automatically, from now on?
values.have: Two ledgers (22 and 27 predictions) covering 2026-11-14..11-17, both verified. A nightly refresh workflow (refresh.yml) already exists but does not seal.
values.missing: Any sealed ledger for 2026-11-13. That slate was already live when the project started, so its nine games — the only ones with official results — can only ever be graded as a backtest, never as a forward test. That gap is permanent for 11/13.
values.how: Add a seal step to the nightly workflow so each day's card is committed before the first tip, and assert the seal date strictly precedes the earliest tip in the set.
values.impact: High. Without pre-registration every future result is a backtest, and a backtest can be tuned after the fact. This is the difference between evidence and a story.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: The 2026-11-17 slate repeats two matchups from the two days before (NYK@TOR also on 11/15, POR@MIN also on 11/16). Is that real, and what does it do to the model?
values.have: Confirmed real: the official game page for 0022600253 reads 'Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 7:30 PM ET' for NYK@TOR. Both pairs appear in the official schedule with distinct game IDs.
values.missing: Whether the model should treat the second meeting differently (rest, preparation, confidence) — we have no evidence either way and no settled games to test it on.
values.how: Leave the games priced normally and flag them (FLAG-ANOM-01 already does); revisit when there is a sample of repeat-matchup results.
values.impact: Two of the five 11/17 games are affected. If repeat matchups behave differently, our lines for them are wrong in a systematic, correctable way.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.question: Do we trust the totals more than the margins? The graded card says the totals improvement is nine times larger.
values.have: On nine games: totals beat the league-mean baseline by 3.30 pts/game, margins beat a zero baseline by 0.36 pts/game. Two >20-point margin misses (GSW@SAS predicted SAS +3.2, actual +38; MEM@NOP predicted MEM by 8.3, actual by 31) drive most of the margin error.
values.missing: Any statistical support (p = 0.40 and p = 0.95), and any idea whether the early-season shrinkage is over-compressing large true team gaps.
values.how: Grade more slates; separately, test the shrinkage weight by re-running the card with lambda swept and see whether the two big misses shrink.
values.impact: If the totals edge is real it is the single most valuable thing found so far, because a total is a market we can price without a win-probability model.

values.question: Which site tree is the product? Six are published from one origin and the Pages setting picks one.
values.have: GitHub Pages is set to build_type 'legacy' from main /, so visitors get the root v1 tree (index.html + pages/). The v2 tree (site/), docs/, dashboard/, originated/, backtest/ and verified/ are all served from the same origin as secondary trees with overlapping content.
values.missing: An owner decision on which is canonical. Prior sessions logged this rather than deciding it, because switching changes every page a reader sees.
values.how: One setting: flip Pages to 'GitHub Actions' to publish the v2 artifact, or keep legacy and retire the others into an archive folder with an index.
values.impact: Until it is decided, a reviewer cannot tell which numbers are current. The root tree now carries every table added this session.

values.question: Official NBA.com standings are now reachable through the page fetcher. Should the third-party ratings source be retired?
values.have: All 30 clubs' W-L read live from nba.com/standings on 2026-11-14, matching the committed snapshot exactly once the 11/13 results are applied. Snapshot: data/raw/standings_2026-11-14_official.json.
values.missing: Official per-game point rates (PS/G, PA/G). nba.com/standings renders the 'Margins & Stats' section, but stats.nba.com endpoints remain unreachable, so the SRS column still comes from basketball-reference and stays flagged FLAG-RAT-01.
values.how: Point the ratings loader at the official standings for W-L (done) and keep the third-party column only for point rates, labelled.

suggestions.title: Site-improvement suggestions — review queue
suggestions.blurb: Each item is written so a reviewer can accept, reject or defer it on its own merits. Nothing is applied silently: the Status column is the record of what has been decided or already built, and every item still stands or falls on its own.
suggestions.source_note: Nothing here has been implemented. Each item is written so it can be accepted, rejected or deferred on its own merits, and the Status column is the record of that decision — not of this session's opinion. Ordered by decision-quality gain per unit of effort.

values.title: Connect a licensed odds feed before anything else
values.problem: Without prices there is no edge, no CLV, no ROI and no way to know whether our line is good; the site can only publish projections and triggers.
values.proposal: Add `nba2/ingest/odds.py` writing dated snapshots to data/raw with book, market, line, price and timestamp; keep closing prices permanently.
values.benefit: Unblocks gates G-02, G-05 on real PnL, G-09, and converts every table from 'projection' to 'decision'.
values.risk: Vendor cost; storing closing lines needs storage rights (Q-18 style check).
values.recommendation: Accept first; nothing else on this list pays as well.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Ingest official game-level results daily
values.problem: σ, HCA, margin/total correlation, prop rates and every backtest all wait on game-level results; today they are fitted from a standings table instead.
values.proposal: Nightly snapshot of final scores by official game ID into data/raw; extend to ≥2 seasons for fitting.
values.benefit: Turns the two fitted constants into measured ones and kills the circularity in G-04.
values.risk: Needs network access from a runner (unavailable in this sandbox).
values.recommendation: Accept with S-01 in the same sprint.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Store point-in-time snapshots, not 'latest' tables
values.problem: An as-of standings table contains future information for games early in its window, which silently inflates any backtest (G-07 currently AT-RISK for exactly this).
values.proposal: Key every snapshot by (as_of_date, game_date) and make the model read only rows with as_of < tip-off.
values.benefit: Makes historical results believable at all; the single most common way a betting model dies.
values.risk: Storage growth; mitigation: parquet or compressed CSV in a data branch.
values.recommendation: Accept before any backtest is quoted on the site.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Ratify thresholds in one sitting
values.problem: Eleven numbers decide which games are actionable and who wins the leaderboard, and all eleven are currently mine.
values.proposal: Owner reviews the Parameters page and signs off (or edits) in a single commit; status flips from 'unratified' to 'ratified' in config.
values.benefit: Makes accountability real instead of implied; a one-hour task that removes a whole class of silent bias.
values.recommendation: Accept now — it blocks 'is this site trustworthy' more than any data purchase.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot

values.title: Preregister strategy trials with a counter
values.problem: G-06 (multiple-testing control) is unpayable while nobody records how many variants were tried; the Deflated Sharpe needs N.
values.proposal: Append every evaluation attempt (id, config hash, timestamp, seed) to data/trials.jsonl; leaderboard reads N from it.
values.benefit: Makes the leaderboard a science instead of a search result; costs ~20 lines.
values.risk: Requires discipline to log failed attempts too — that is the point.
values.recommendation: Accept; pair with a rule 'no evaluation without registration'.

values.title: Render 'why is this blank' on every empty cell
values.problem: A blank cell reads as 'no data' but not as 'which missing input, and what would fill it'.
values.proposal: The generator already attaches flag ids to blanks (see the strict rule in nba2/provenance.py::make_row): render the flag id as a tooltip on each blank cell, linking to its entry on the Flagged page.
values.benefit: Turns every gap into a one-click work item for the reviewer instead of a mystery.
values.risk: Adds ~40 lines of build logic; must stay in sync with the flag registry.
values.recommendation: Accept — cheap and it is what the Flagged page exists for.

values.title: Staleness banner with an explicit expiry
values.problem: Lines published from a 3-day-old snapshot look identical to fresh ones; nothing on the page says 'stop'.
values.proposal: Header banner computing age of snapshot vs a policy max age (e.g. 24h), turning red past expiry and disabling the picks tab.
values.benefit: Prevents the most expensive realistic failure: betting yesterday's number today.
values.risk: Needs the scheduled rebuild (S-16) to be meaningful.
values.recommendation: Accept with S-16.

values.title: Replace third-party ratings with an official snapshot
values.problem: Every line currently derives from Basketball-Reference values (PS/G, PA/G, SRS) because the official endpoint was unreachable here; that is flagged (FLAG-RAT-01) but it is the load-bearing wall.
values.proposal: When R-104 is possible, ingest official team stats at a fixed daily time and delete the third-party file; keep both during a parallel period to measure drift.
values.benefit: Removes the largest single caveat on the site and satisfies the 'official source' rule literally.
values.risk: Official endpoint access/licensing (see Q-18's twin problem).
values.recommendation: Accept after S-02.

values.title: Structured injury-PDF parser instead of text extraction
values.problem: 17 of 91 rows needed team attribution from block continuation because the PDF table breaks across pages (FLAG-INJ-01).
values.proposal: Parse the report with a table-aware reader keyed on the Game Date column, and store page/row coordinates for each record.
values.benefit: Kills the attribution caveat and lets the site assert completeness ('all 7 pages parsed').
values.risk: PDF layout changes without notice mid-season.
values.recommendation: Accept; it is a correctness fix, not polish.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Add a game-day re-issue build (T-0) alongside the T-3 build
values.problem: Injury reports for future days are 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' — proven this session — so a 3-day-ahead line is structurally injury-blind.
values.proposal: Publish two sealed snapshots per day (T-3 and T-0 after the 13:00 ET report) and show the delta between them as the injury signal.
values.benefit: Converts a weakness into a measurable quantity: how much our line moves on availability news, which is a strategy family of its own.
values.recommendation: Accept — the best idea on this list for model quality per unit of data.

values.title: Show per-line contribution of every input
values.problem: 'San Antonio -4.5' is opaque: nobody can see how much is rating gap, shrinkage, HCA or injury-blindness.
values.proposal: Add a decomposition column (SRS gap ×λ, raw-margin gap ×λ, HCA, injury adj) per line, computed not asserted.
values.benefit: Reviewers can disagree with a component instead of the whole number; that is how a model gets better.
values.recommendation: Accept.

values.title: Bankroll/staking page with the actual policy applied
values.problem: Stakes are pinned to 0% by rule until prices exist, which is correct but explains nothing to a reviewer.
values.proposal: A page showing the staking maths with the current caps and what a bet would look like at each available price once S-01 lands.
values.benefit: Makes the 0% legible as a policy rather than a gap.
values.risk: Must not become a calculator that implies a recommendation.
values.recommendation: Accept with a disclaimer requirement.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Per-game chart: rating gap vs line, with the disagreement band
values.problem: Tables answer 'what number' but not 'how near the decision boundary is this game'.
values.proposal: Small multiples drawn client-side from site.json; the band is the sensitivity box, so a narrow bar = fragile line.
values.benefit: Fragile picks become visible without reading the stability column.
values.risk: Chart code must render the same numbers as the table or we get two truths; generate from the same JSON.
values.recommendation: Defer until S-01/S-02 so there is something worth drawing.

values.title: Table ergonomics: sticky headers, density toggle, CSV export
values.problem: The 31-row lines table and 91-row injury table are the working surface; today they scroll freely and cannot be exported.
values.proposal: Sticky thead, a compact-density class, and a per-table 'download CSV' that includes the source column.
values.benefit: Reviewers can work offline without losing provenance — export keeps the source link per row.
values.recommendation: Accept.

values.title: Accessibility and print path
values.problem: A dense analytical dashboard with no ARIA table semantics and no print stylesheet is hard to review with colleagues.
values.proposal: scope=headers, caption elements, focus styles, and a print stylesheet that keeps source URLs.
values.benefit: Reviewable in a meeting, which is where decisions actually happen.
values.recommendation: Accept.

source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Scheduled rebuild with a freshness gate
values.problem: The site updates only when a session commits; the numbers are a frozen 2026-11-13 snapshot.
values.proposal: Daily Actions workflow that re-ingests, rebuilds, re-seals, and fails (not publishes) if any official source is unreachable.
values.benefit: Ends the 'is this current?' question. Failure to fetch becomes visible instead of silent staleness.
values.risk: Runner needs network to the official endpoints; a failing schedule must not publish a stale site.
values.recommendation: Accept once S-02 exists.

source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Compliance framing on the front page
values.problem: A public page that prints spreads, parlays and staking language reads as betting advice; today the notice is a footer line.
values.proposal: Front-page notice: research tool, no guarantees, 21+/jurisdiction responsibility, links to problem-gambling help.
values.benefit: Reduces real-world harm and the risk of the site being read as a tipster service.
values.recommendation: Accept.

source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Keep the sealed ledger in git, not a database
values.problem: A leaderboard is only credible if predictions cannot be edited after the fact.
values.proposal: Keep the current design: canonical JSON + sha256, committed with the site build; never rewrite history.
values.benefit: Auditable by anyone with the repo, with no infrastructure to trust.
values.risk: Git history bloat over a season; mitigate with monthly squash archives.
values.recommendation: Already applied; keep unless a DB is required for scale.

values.title: Publish from a build directory instead of the repository root
values.problem: `path: '.'` makes every committed file public, including data snapshots and anything a future session commits by mistake.
values.proposal: Build to `site/` (HTML + assets + data/site.json) and publish that directory only.
values.benefit: Reduces accidental disclosure; keeps the public surface explicit.
values.effort: M (changes every relative link + breaks current live URLs unless redirected)
values.risk: URL churn; needs a redirect plan for the already-live root pages.
values.recommendation: Defer — real improvement, but it breaks existing links and none of the currently committed files are sensitive.

values.title: Stop writing narrative into empty analysis columns
values.problem: The temptation this site is built to resist: a 'game flow' page with adjectives where pace numbers should be.
values.proposal: Keep policy as code (blank + flag is the only permitted empty state) and add a lint rule that fails any prose-only analysis column.
values.benefit: The property that makes everything else on the site usable as evidence.
values.recommendation: Already applied via make_row + lint; do not weaken it under time pressure.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Ship a 'Live verification' page that re-grades the site against today's official pages
values.problem: The site could only claim freshness by asserting it. Nothing on it re-reads an official page at render time, so a stale record and a correct record looked identical (proof: 18 of 30 team records are stale right now while the page still shows MATCH).
values.proposal: A dedicated page, generated from audit/<date>/ captures, that lists each official page read today, what it proved or contradicted, and every published row that no longer matches. Each row links the official URL it was checked against.
values.benefit: Turns 'verified' from a claim into an artefact a reader can audit in ten seconds, and makes staleness visible instead of silent.
values.risk: Needs a disciplined capture ritual; a page built from an old capture is worse than none, so the page prints the fetch timestamp on every row.
values.recommendation: Accept. This is the highest decision-quality gain per unit of effort on the site.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Publish the true sample size next to every hit rate, never the inflated one
values.problem: The graded picks read as 8-0. They are 4-0: four games were each bet by two strategies, so a reader scanning the strategy tables sees double the evidence that exists.
values.proposal: Every hit-rate table carries both numbers - 'signal rows graded' and 'distinct games' - and any strategy with fewer than the ratified minimum shows 'insufficient evidence' in place of a ranking.
values.benefit: Removes the single most common way a small sample is made to look like skill.
values.risk: None; it can only reduce claims.
values.recommendation: Accept and make it a lint rule: a hit rate without its n cannot render.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Score the model against named naive baselines before it scores itself
values.problem: The site reports model accuracy without the baselines that would beat it. On the nine graded games the model's winner accuracy (5/9) equals a net-rating baseline (5/9) and loses to 'always pick home' (7/9).
values.proposal: Every accuracy number renders beside three free baselines computed from the same frozen inputs: home always, higher net rating, higher SRS. A strategy cannot be ranked above the best baseline it fails to beat.
values.benefit: Kills the 'my model is 56%' claim that a coin plus home-court advantage already produces.
values.risk: On small n the baseline will sometimes win by luck - which is the point, and the page says so.
values.recommendation: Accept; make 'beats the best baseline at p<0.05' a gate condition rather than a comment.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Make the suggestions page an explicit decision queue with owner actions
values.problem: Suggestions were a list of proposals with a status string. A reviewer could not accept, reject or defer one in a way that changed anything, so the queue's state was decorative.
values.proposal: Each suggestion renders with four fields: evidence (a live source link), what changes if accepted, effort, and an owner action of accept / reject / defer. The page states plainly that nothing has been implemented on the owner's behalf and that accept is the only state that authorises work.
values.benefit: The owner can choose a path before any of it is built, which is exactly what the brief asks for.
values.risk: None; it is a presentation contract.
values.recommendation: Accept.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Add a staleness gate to the build, not just a timestamp to the page
values.problem: Every page prints an as-of date, but no build fails when the date is old. The stamp is honest and inert.
values.proposal: nba2/v2/check.py fails when a table's newest capture is older than a per-table limit (records 24h, injuries to the next filing, prices 15m), and the Pages workflow cannot publish a build that fails it.
values.benefit: Makes 'up to date' enforceable, which is the only way it survives contact with a busy week.
values.risk: A stale official source would block deploys; mitigated by letting the gate downgrade to a loud banner after N hours rather than a hard fail on the whole site.
values.recommendation: Accept, after Q-23 is answered (the limits are the owner's risk appetite, not mine).

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Fix the spread-sign inversion in the S2 selections before any of it is graded by a human
values.problem: S2_SpreadValue emits 'POR +6.0' for a game where the same file's label says 'POR -6.0' and the model has POR as a 6.07-point favourite. A reader taking that at face value takes the wrong side of the model's own number.
values.proposal: Correct the away-side sign in nba2/picks.py so a selection always names the side with the points. Regenerate picks.json. Do not touch data/raw/ledger (the sealed ledgers are immutable).
values.benefit: Removes a defect that silently inverts a published recommendation.
values.risk: picks.json is another session's artefact; the change is logged here for its owner rather than made unilaterally.
values.recommendation: Accept and assign to the owner of nba2/picks.py.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Retire the unreachable v1 tree instead of maintaining two generators
values.problem: Probed on 2026-11-14: exactly one tree is published (site/). The root v1 tree returns 404 for every page — pages/session-audit.html and pages/executive-summary.html were both checked — yet ci.yml still regenerates, lints and parity-checks it on every push, and it carries records that are stale since the 11/13 finals.
values.proposal: Move root index.html, pages/**, flagged.html and data/site.json under archive/ with a dated note explaining what each was, drop the v1 parity step from ci.yml, and delete nothing.
values.benefit: One number per question is the precondition for every other claim on the site.
values.risk: Breaks inbound links to the old trees; the redirect pages fix that.
values.recommendation: Accept, as the first integration action (this is Q-27).

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Run the test suite against a fresh clone before trusting 'committed == rebuilt'
values.problem: The v1 determinism test passed on every working copy and failed on every clean clone, because two published values depended on the presence of a previous build. Local runs rewrote the artefact and then compared it with itself.
values.proposal: Add a CI job that clones the repository into a temp directory, runs the suite there, then rebuilds and asserts a clean git status. The publish-parity workflow now does the rebuild half; the clone half is the part that caught this.
values.benefit: Turns a class of silent, self-erasing test passes into a failure at PR time.
values.risk: Adds ~30s of CI; no production risk.
values.recommendation: Accept — this is the check that found F-029.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Put the graded-results card on the landing page, above the category grid
values.problem: The landing page opened with model parameters (sigma, HCA) and tier counts, which are the least decision-relevant numbers on the site. The one measurement against real outcomes was buried.
values.proposal: Render a 'Graded against official results' block at the top of the dashboard with the four numbers that matter (margin MAE, total MAE, winner calls, games needed for power) and a link to the full card.
values.benefit: A reader learns in five seconds what the model has been proven to do, and what the sample can support, before meeting any parameter.
values.risk: None; the block is generated from the same graded JSON.
values.recommendation: Accept — implemented this session (session arena/3681def8-nba2).

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Render every URL-valued table cell as a clickable link
values.problem: The slate table's official-game-page column and the graded card's source column printed verified URLs as plain text, so a reviewer had to copy-paste them. Raised earlier as FLAG-AUD-01 and left open.
values.proposal: In the table renderer, detect a cell whose entire value is an http(s) URL and emit an anchor. The value, the provenance badge and the row's own source column are unchanged.
values.benefit: Manual verification becomes one click. 89 cells across the slate and graded tables become clickable without touching a single value.
values.risk: None to data; external links already open with rel=noopener.
values.recommendation: Accept — implemented this session; FLAG-AUD-01 can now be closed.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Seal every slate before its first tip, in the nightly job
values.problem: Nothing was sealed for 2026-11-13, the only slate with official results, so the first graded card is a backtest and can never become a forward test (FLAG-GRADE-01, Q-31).
values.proposal: Add a seal step to .github/workflows/refresh.yml that commits a ledger for the next slate, and make seal_predictions assert that the seal timestamp strictly precedes the earliest tip in the set.
values.benefit: Every future result becomes pre-registered evidence instead of a story that can be revised after the fact. This is the cheapest real improvement available.
values.risk: Low; fails closed (no seal, no published picks) which is the correct behaviour.
values.recommendation: Accept first among the open items — it is the only one that makes future evidence trustworthy.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Decide on one canonical site tree and archive the other five
values.problem: Six trees (root/pages, site/, docs/, dashboard/, originated/, backtest/) publish from one origin with overlapping and sometimes conflicting numbers. A reviewer cannot tell which is current (Q-34).
values.proposal: Keep the root v1 tree, move the others under a single /archive/ path with an index that states each tree's as-of date and why it was kept, and link them from one place on the dashboard.
values.benefit: One current answer per question, with the history one click away instead of mixed into the navigation.
values.effort: M — moves plus an index page
values.risk: Breaks inbound links to the moved trees; needs redirects or a clear index.
values.recommendation: Accept, but as an owner decision — it changes what every visitor sees.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Investigate rating shrinkage after two >20-point margin misses
values.problem: GSW@SAS (predicted SAS +3.2, actual +38) and MEM@NOP (predicted MEM by 8.3, actual by 31) contributed 57 of the 117 total margin error on nine games.
values.proposal: Re-run the 2026-11-13 card with the shrinkage weight swept across a grid and publish the resulting MAE curve, so the choice is measured rather than assumed.
values.benefit: Either confirms the current weight or finds a cheap accuracy gain; either way it retires one of the unratified parameters.
values.effort: S — the grading script already exists; add a sweep
values.risk: Fitting shrinkage on the same nine games would be overfitting; report the curve, do not pick the minimum from it.
values.recommendation: Accept, with the explicit rule that no parameter is chosen from these nine games.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Make the nightly refresh ingest official standings and final scores
values.problem: The refresh workflow fetches the slate and injury report but not the official standings or completed-game scores, so ratings and settlement stay manual.
values.proposal: Add two steps: nba.com/standings -> data/raw/standings_<date>_official.json, and nba.com/schedule finals -> data/raw/finals_<date>.json, then run settle.
values.benefit: Closes the loop unattended: official records in, graded cards out, every morning.
values.effort: M — two ingest functions plus the settle step
values.risk: The page fetcher is the only working retrieval path in this environment; the workflow runner may reach the same hosts directly, which should be probed first.
values.recommendation: Accept after the reachability probe in CC-FRESH-03 confirms the runner can reach nba.com.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Group the navigation by the decision each page supports
values.problem: Twenty flat sidebar links in file order gave no signal about what to read first.
values.proposal: Group into Decide / Measure / Inputs / Governance / Project, with a one-line description per category, and mirror the grouping on the dashboard.
values.benefit: The site reads as a dashboard with an order of operations rather than a listing.
values.effort: S — data structure in the builder plus CSS
values.risk: None; every existing page keeps its URL.
values.recommendation: Accept — implemented this session.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Make the existing nightly ingest actually run, and extend it to the v2 results history
values.problem: A nightly ingest workflow already exists (.github/workflows/refresh.yml, on a cron schedule) and has NEVER executed — gh run list for it is empty, which is why the repo's own freshness check (CC-FRESH-03) reports 'the schedule is armed but nothing has run'. It also targets the v1 pipeline (sealed-window injury PDFs, data/raw/finals_*.json, v1 settlement), not the v2 results history in data/raw/history/. The consequence is visible: the results log was 28 games short for a day and the published standings were a full day stale, with nothing on the site able to detect either.
values.proposal: Confirm the cron schedule is enabled on the default branch (a scheduled workflow only starts firing after it is merged to the default branch once), then extend the job to append each completed date to data/raw/history/ and assert the per-date game count against the nba.com day-strip calendar and the game count implied by the standings. Fail the run on any disagreement.
values.benefit: Makes the window impossible to fall behind silently, and turns the standings into a permanent cross-check on the results log.
values.risk: Low. The workflow is already written and fail-closed; only the extension to data/raw/history/ is new.
values.recommendation: Accept — the schedule is already armed, so the cheapest possible fix is confirming it fires.

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Capture per-player game logs so the last hard blocker can close
values.problem: Every player-level correlation on the site is BLOCKED, the player-props page cannot price anything, the minutes-and-production half of the injuries page cannot be filled, and strategy S7 has never generated a bet. All four fail for the same missing input.
values.proposal: Ingest per-player game logs (minutes, points, rebounds, assists, opponent) for at least the players who appear on an injury report. Start with the injury-report population to bound the cost.
values.benefit: Unblocks the last data dependency in the brief. Everything else on the site can be built, measured and settled with what is already committed.
values.risk: Needs a licensed feed or a scheduled scrape; player-level data is rate-limited more aggressively.
values.recommendation: Accept — it is the only remaining hard blocker (mirrors v2 suggestion SG-30).

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Decide which tree GitHub Pages serves, and retire the other
values.problem: RESOLVED by measurement, 2026-11-14. The GitHub Pages API reports build_type 'legacy' with source 'main' path '/', which reads as if the v1 root tree were live. Fetching the live URL shows otherwise: /strategy-lab.html resolves with full v2 content, and that file exists only under site/. So the live site already IS the single clean v2 tree, and no setting change is needed. The API field and the served tree disagree, which is itself worth recording.
values.proposal: Pick the v2 tree as the single published site, point Pages at the pages.yml workflow, and move the root-level v1 pages under archive/ with a dated note.
values.benefit: One site, one set of numbers, no chance of a reader landing on the stale one.
values.risk: Low, but it is a repository setting change that only the owner can make — this session cannot push it and should not guess.
values.recommendation: No action required — measured, not assumed. Do NOT 'fix' the Pages setting on the strength of the API field alone; re-fetch the live URL first, because the field contradicts what is served.
values.status: implemented this session (verified by fetching the live URL)

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Replace the flat 300-bet gate with a power calculation per strategy
values.problem: Gate G7 applies one round number to all seven strategies. But the parlay strategies have far more variance per bet than the side strategies, so the same n gives them a much wider interval — the bar is not equally strict across types, and 300 was chosen before any data existed to check it.
values.proposal: Simulate each strategy's own settled bet stream to get its bet-to-bet correlation, then set the required n per strategy. The lab already computes every Wilson interval and distance to base rate needed to do this.
values.benefit: Makes the gate a measurement instead of a round number, and tells each strategy how far it has to go.
values.risk: Low. Changes when strategies become rank-eligible, so it should be published with its derivation.
values.recommendation: Accept (mirrors v2 suggestion SG-26).

source.name: COORDINATION.md
source.class_label: Derived in-repo from a verified snapshot
source.note: Session claims, conflict log, irregularity findings.

values.title: Publish the parlay price with its measured correlation, and print the naive product beside it
values.problem: The same-game correlation is now measured (+0.0393, 95% CI -0.113 to +0.190, n=167), but the site still withholds a parlay price entirely. The honest position is no longer 'we do not know the correlation' but 'we do not know it precisely' — and withholding the price hides the error bar rather than showing it.
values.proposal: Price every parlay with the measured rho using the bivariate-normal pricer already implemented and tested in nba2/v2/strategy_lab.py, and print the naive product on the same row with the interval between them.
values.benefit: Turns an unpriced section into a priced one, with the uncertainty visible instead of implied.
values.risk: The interval is wide, so the price must ship with the interval on the same row or it will be read as more precise than it is.
values.recommendation: Defer until S-29 has grown the sample past ~500 games, then accept (mirrors SG-28).

surfaces.title: Everything published in this repository, and who made it
surfaces.blurb: Six independent site layers now exist in one repo because six sessions worked in parallel, three of them merged while this page was being written. This is the honest map: which one is canonical, where the others live, and that none was deleted to shrink the count. The durable fix is structural — own a directory and a data namespace, as `originated/**` did — not a stricter merge rule.

x3way.title: Three originated lines for the same games — and how much of the gap is convention
x3way.blurb: Mean |gap| across 31 games: 2.9 pts as published, 2.7 pts once session 3's own injury adjustment is stripped out using the fields it published. The reduction is the point: two teams reading the same official data and disagreeing by 6 points are usually disagreeing about a *parameter*, and a parameter nobody ratified is not evidence.

graded.title: Graded card — 2026-11-13: our line vs the official final score
graded.blurb: Nine games, priced from the committed ratings snapshot that predates every tip, scored against the official NBA.com finals. This is the first card in the repository graded against real results rather than against itself. It is a walk-forward backtest, not a pre-registered ledger — see FLAG-GRADE-01 before reading anything into it.

values.title: Re-ingest the injury report at its latest official revision
values.problem: The published injury rows are the 16:15 ET revision; three newer official revisions existed the same evening (17:15, 18:15, 19:15) with 12 status changes and 32 added rows.
values.proposal: Before each pick run, fetch the newest official PDF revision, re-run the capture→delta→build cycle, and stamp the revision time on the Injuries page.
values.benefit: Lines and rotation notes stop being priced off a superseded designation list; the currency flag closes.
values.effort: Low — the parser and delta already exist (audit/parse_injury_0715.py).
values.risk: Low — snapshots stay immutable; each revision becomes its own committed capture.
values.recommendation: Done for the nightly cycle by the 2026-11-14 refresh (nba2/pipeline/refresh.py + .github/workflows/refresh.yml); keep this item as the reminder for the game-day 13:00 ET report.

values.title: Settle the sealed ledger as soon as finals exist
values.problem: At proposal time settlement had run but measured nothing: data/settlement.json carried settled_at 2026-11-14T00:58Z with finals_snapshot null, so every leaderboard score, bet count and reward cell was blank and the gates stayed blocked — correctly, because the sealed games of 11/14–17 had not finished.
values.proposal: After each game day, commit data/raw/finals_<date>.json (official final scores, source-linked) and re-run python -m nba2.pipeline.settle.
values.benefit: First real measurement of line error and calibration — the 'remove luck' step becomes data, not design.
values.effort: Low — settle.py is written, tested, and already produces the pending record.
values.risk: None if finals come from official box scores; never impute a score.
values.recommendation: Run it after 11/14's games are final, then after each subsequent game day.
values.status: partially done — the finals ingest chain is live and verified (finals_all.json carries the nine official 11/13 finals; 0 of 49 sealed games have been played as of 2026-11-14); the nightly ingest job now fetches, merges and settles each game day automatically

values.title: Pick one canonical site tree
values.problem: Six site trees now ship from one repo (root+pages/, docs/, dashboard/, originated/, verified/, backtest/); a reviewer can find different numbers on different trees.
values.proposal: Owner designates one canonical tree; the others get a banner linking to it. Candidate criteria: mechanical verifier + no unverified numbers (originated/ has a 24-check verifier; root+pages/ has the provenance lint over 1,100 rows; backtest/ has its own verify_backtest).
values.benefit: One truth surface; removes the reconciliation burden from every future session.
values.effort: Medium — mostly a decision plus five banner edits.
values.risk: Low — nothing is deleted; trees stay for audit.
values.recommendation: Decide before the next data refresh so only one tree is refreshed.
values.status: DECIDED 2026-11-14, CORRECTED the same day after direct probing (merge reconciliation log, COORDINATION.md): the live URL serves the v2 site/ artifact (pages/session-audit.html returns 404; the v2 dashboard serves at the root URL) — the Pages API's build_type: legacy does NOT describe the served artifact, so the earlier 'root+pages/ is canonical' claim was wrong. What remains for the owner is S-27/Q-27: archive the root tree or keep it maintained as the sealed-ledger and settlement surface (it stays CI-verified meanwhile: provenance lint over 1,143 rows, semantic cross-check 83 pass / 0 fail). values.statement: The close-game and blowout-game split columns are internally inconsistent AT THE TEAM LEVEL: for 18 of the 30 clubs the close and blowout rows together account for more games than the club has played (ATL shows 13 close+blowout games in a 12-game record, MEM 12 in 11, DET 12 in 11). The league-wide sums DO balance (close 99=99, blowout 88=88), so a league-level check alone would have passed - the check has to be per team. These columns are therefore NOT used for any model parameter and are left blank in the luck table: a split that contradicts the games played cannot support a per-team luck claim. The cause is the text extraction of the source table (blank/merged cells), not necessarily the source itself.
values.action: Re-extract the close/blowout columns from the source table row by row, or drop them from the snapshot. Do not publish them until every club satisfies close+blowout <= games played (owner decision tracked as suggestion S-34, renumbered from the queue-fragment S-26).
